knowledge.purpose: Side navigation for a documentation site or an app section: a tree of links and collapsible groups held in its own props, with the page in view marked.
useCases: Documentation sidebar: groups of pages with nested sub-pages
Settings or admin section navigation beside the content
Handbook or course outline with chapters and lessons
antiPatterns: The site's top navigation: use layout.navbar
A file or data hierarchy the visitor explores: that is a tree view, not navigation
Hand-written links in a layout.container for the same tree: the sidebar marks the current page and opens its group
knowledge.implementation: A <nav> landmark (named by title or navLabel) over nested lists. `items` is the tree: each entry is {label, href?, children?, open?}: a link, a group (children), or a page that is also a group. A group without href is a toggle button carrying its label; a group with href is its link with a chevron toggle beside it, named in the app's words (ui.tree.expand / ui.tree.collapse). Toggles carry aria-expanded and aria-controls; a closed group's entries are hidden. `activeHref` is the page in view: its link carries aria-current="page" (the same route matcher as navbar and app-rail) and every group above it opens. `open: true` starts a group open; `collapsible: false` shows every group open with no toggle (group labels become small headings). Each entry's href arrives in the router's form, as the host rewrites href members; in the editor a click reports the destination instead of leaving the page. Everything is reachable with Tab, Enter and Space. On a phone (below 768px) the tree folds behind one button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, named by the title or the app word ui.sidebar.menu (English "Menu" when unset); CSS decides, so the first frame is right at every width, and choosing a link folds it again. foldOnPhone: false always shows the tree.

props.name: items
props.type: [{label, href?, open?, children?: [{label, href?, open?, children?}]}]

match.description: exact (default): current only on its own address. prefix: also marks the section on every page below it ("/guides" on "/guides/records"); aria-current="page" stays on the exact page.
exact (default): current only on its own address. prefix: also marks the section on every page below it ("/guides" on "/guides/records"); aria-current="page" stays on the exact page.

jsonSchema.description: The tree. An entry with children is a group; with href it is also a page. Deeper levels take the same shape.
A heading over the tree ("Documentation"); it names the navigation landmark too.
The navigation landmark's name when there is no title, or a different one.
The page in view: its link is marked current and the groups above it open.
Groups open and close (default). false shows every group open, with no toggle.
Below 768px the tree folds behind one button (named by the title, else the app word ui.sidebar.menu), so a long tree does not sit above every page. false always shows the tree.

tokens.description: Fill behind the link to the page in view.

tokens.name: currentWeight
tokens.description: Weight of the link to the page in view and of the section it is in.

tokens.description: Space above and below a row’s text.

tokens.name: itemPaddingInline
tokens.description: Space left and right of a row’s text.

tokens.name: depthIndent
tokens.description: How far a row’s text moves in per level of depth.

tokens.name: nestIndent
tokens.description: How far a nested list sits in from its parent.

tokens.name: nestPadding
tokens.description: Space between a nested list’s guide line and its rows.

tokens.description: Thickness of the guide line beside a nested list; 0 draws none.

tokens.description: Colour of the guide line beside a nested list.

tokens.description: Thickness of the edge on a row’s left; 0 draws none.
